finding: §2.1 asserts that two identically-authored roles differing only in id produce prompts "identical modulo the role id and the output path", and §7 item 2 pins that as a test. This contradicts the per-role file inliner the spec never says it changes: inside generateRoleAuditPrompts a single `inlinerDone` latch gives the FIRST emitted role whose file set fits the reading budget the whole file contents plus the `filesComplete` framing ("## Affected Files (complete)"), while every later role gets named paths only. Two identically-authored roles present in the same corpus therefore differ by an inlined-content block and a different framing paragraph — a difference caused by emission position, not by id dispatch — so the stated property is false and the pinned test cannot pass as written.

resolved.evidence: §2.9 added, stating that §2 changes neither the per-role inliner latch nor the role-id-derived slug truncation, and pinning the equality claim against a fixture that holds both constant: two separate audit invocations, each with a single non-spec-coverage role, ids of equal length. §2.1's sentence was rewritten to the narrower claim (no id other than spec-coverage changes prompt construction) and §7 item 2 now names that fixture.

suggestion: State the comparison's scope: either compare the two roles across two separate audit invocations in which each is the only non-spec-coverage role (so both are the inliner), or define the equality modulo the inlined-content block and framing as well as the role id and output path. Say explicitly that §2 does not change the §10.7 per-role inliner.

finding: §2.6 requires the affected-files header to be rendered from "the cap actually applied to that role's list" and to state "how many of how many are shown" when the pre-cap set was larger, but neither value reaches the renderer. buildRolePrompt receives only `files []engine.AuditFileEntry`; the applied cap is a package constant in engine (AuditFileCap / CodeFileCap) and the pre-cap count exists only as the length of filterAuditUniverse's local slice, which SelectAuditFiles discards. §2.4 item 2 simultaneously pins SelectAuditFiles to return "the spec-coverage list and the shared code-file list only", closing the obvious channel. The literal header text is also never given, yet §7 item 9 asserts on it, so two tasks would each invent a different string.

resolved.evidence: §2.5 names the carrier: AuditFileSelection gains SpecCoverageTotal and CodeFilesTotal, and buildRolePrompt takes the applied cap plus the pre-cap total. §2.6 pins the two literal forms exactly — '## Affected Files (max 10)' and '## Affected Files (10 of 34, max 10)' — so §2.6 and §7 item 10 assert the same string instead of two tasks inventing different ones.

suggestion: Name the carrier and the literal: e.g. add a pre-cap count (and per-list cap) to AuditFileSelection or pass `cap int, preCapTotal int` into buildRolePrompt, and pin the exact rendered forms — e.g. `## Affected Files (max 10)` when nothing was truncated and `## Affected Files (10 of 34, max 10)` when it was — so §2.6 and §7 item 9 assert the same string.

finding: §2.8 presents itself as the complete inventory ("Three committed tests encode the behavior being removed ... and one must be widened"), but at least two more committed assertions break and are unnamed, so the change lands red with no spec-sanctioned update and no §7 item covering them. (a) TestAuditPrompts_BodyOrderAndEmbedding (internal/cli/audit_prompts_test.go:65) asserts `assert.NotContains(t, sec, "## Project Context")` — literally the id gate §2.3 removes — and it also pins the literal header `## Affected Files (max 20)` at line 33, which §2.6 rewrites. (b) TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted (internal/engine/auditfiles_test.go:125) asserts `assert.Empty(t, sel.Security)`; §2.8 item 3 promises the remaining assertions in that file are "renamed mechanically to CodeFiles and CodeFileCap", but this one references a deleted field and must be deleted, not renamed — a mechanical rename leaves it uncompilable.

resolved.evidence: §2.8 rewritten as an exhaustive inventory against a named search (sel.Security, selectSecurity, HeadReader, roleSecurity, roleMaintainability, '## Project Context', and the literal '## Affected Files (max 20)'), now covering seven items. TestAuditPrompts_BodyOrderAndEmbedding is item 6 with both required edits, and TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted is item 4 with its sel.Security line deleted rather than renamed.

suggestion: Add TestAuditPrompts_BodyOrderAndEmbedding to §2.8 with its two required edits (drop the security Project-Context negative assertion; state what the affected-files header assertion becomes under §2.6), and amend §2.8 item 3 to say that residual `sel.Security` assertions outside the two named tests (auditfiles_test.go:125) are deleted rather than renamed. State the inventory as exhaustive against a named search (e.g. every committed reference to Security/selectSecurity/HeadReader/roleMaintainability-gated prompt text) so a reader can verify completeness.

finding: §3.4 puts the eject advisory on "the human/info channel alongside the existing success message" and §7 item 14 asserts the substring appears while the stdout JSON keys stay `{ejected, domain}`. Both output.Info and output.Success return early when jsonMode is set, and Configure sets `jsonMode = forceJSON || !isatty.IsTerminal(os.Stdout.Fd())` — so any run whose stdout is a pipe (every agent invocation, and every existing test that captures stdout through runTP) emits nothing on that channel. The advisory is therefore invisible in exactly the case §7 item 14 must observe it, and invisible to the agent audience the release is written for; the test cannot pass without changing Info's gating (which would alter every other command's output) or writing the line through a different channel.

resolved.evidence: Confirmed against internal/output/output.go: both Info and Success return early on jsonMode, and jsonMode is set whenever stdout is not a terminal — so the round-1 'info channel' answer made the advisory invisible in every piped and agent-driven run and untestable through runTP. §3.4 now routes it through a new output.Notice primitive: stderr, suppressed by --quiet, not suppressed by JSON mode, documented as the channel for a one-time advisory about project-owned data a command just wrote. §7 item 15 asserts it specifically with stdout piped.

suggestion: Pin the channel: either state that the advisory bypasses the JSON-mode gate (a direct stderr write, with the observable consequence that stderr is no longer empty in JSON mode), or accept TTY-only emission and rewrite §7 item 14 to assert it through a TTY/injected-writer seam rather than a piped stdout capture. Also say explicitly whether `--quiet` suppression is the only gate.

finding: §7 item 2 (and the §2.1 claim it encodes — "prompts are likewise identical modulo the role id and the output path") cannot be asserted as written, and would fail against a correct implementation. Two mechanisms break the substitution equality: (1) `fileCheckItems` builds each item id as `file-<role-id>-<slug>` where the slug is `slugifySubject(path + " " + "Apply the <roleID> role rules to <path>")` truncated to 40 chars — so `security` and a shorter/longer id truncate at different points in the subject and no string replacement of the role id maps one prompt onto the other (e.g. `plain-go-apply-the-security-role-rules-t` vs `plain-go-apply-the-sec-role-rules-to-pla`); (2) within one audit run only the first emitted role inlines its file contents (the per-role inliner sets `inlinerDone` once), so two roles in the same corpus differ by whole inlined file bodies plus the framing that flags them complete. The spec also never says whether the two ids are compared within one corpus/run or across two single-role invocations, which decides both points.

resolved.evidence: Same defect as the architect's prompt-equality finding, fixed together in §2.9 — and this finding supplied the second mechanism (the 40-character slug truncation making id substitution non-bijective for unequal-length ids), which is why the fixture pins ids of equal length rather than only pinning the inliner.

suggestion: Pin the fixture and the normalization: state that the comparison is between two separate audit invocations, each with a one-role corpus (so the inliner applies identically), and that equality holds after normalizing the role id, the output path, and the role-id-derived item-id slug — or restrict the assertion to ids of equal length and say so. Restate §2.1's sentence with the same qualifiers so the prose and the test agree.

finding: §2.1 and §2.3 remove the last three readers of the `roleSecurity` and `roleMaintainability` constants (audit_roles.go lines 54/55, 220, 286/288), leaving both constants unreferenced anywhere in the repo, yet the spec's removal inventory (§2.4) enumerates only `internal/engine/auditfiles.go` symbols. Two consequences: the `unused` linter is enabled in `.golangci.yml`, so unreferenced unexported constants fail the quality gate this release must pass; and keeping `roleSecurity = "security"` / `roleMaintainability = "..."` as named constants preserves in code the very id coupling the release is titled after removing.

resolved.evidence: §2.1 now states that the roleSecurity and roleMaintainability constants are deleted with their switch arms and that roleSpecCoverage remains as the one reserved id, so the change does not leave unreferenced constants for the enabled `unused` linter to fail the gate on.

suggestion: Extend the removal inventory to `roleSecurity` and `roleMaintainability` in `internal/cli/audit_roles.go`, keeping only `roleSpecCoverage`, which remains the single reserved id.

finding: The PASS-when-out-of-domain disposition is a per-role constant, but §2.2 puts it inside every item's expected_evidence, which fileCheckItems generates once per selected file. Today that field is the 3-word `inspect file: <path>`; a sentence-length instruction is repeated CodeFileCap (10) times per role, and each item is emitted twice per prompt object (the JSON array inside the prompt body's `## Checklist` block and again in the prompt's `checklist_items` field), so tp's own 3 non-spec-coverage auditors would restate the identical wording up to 60 times per audit round, and again on every required clean round. --compact does not blunt it: compactAuditChecklist truncates only `text` (at 80 chars) and drops file_summary, never expected_evidence. The prompt already carries a once-per-role place for exactly this kind of statement — renderAuditOutputSchema() plus outputContractInstruction() — where one copy is equally 'part of the emitted contract, not left to sub-agent judgment', and where it does not scale with the file count.

resolved.evidence: §2.2 restructured on this finding's argument: the disposition rule is rendered once per prompt as a fixed '## Disposition' paragraph after the checklist block, and expected_evidence stays the existing short 'inspect file: <path>'. §7 item 8 pins the once-per-prompt placement by asserting no expected_evidence value contains the word PASS.

suggestion: State the disposition rule once per prompt in the audit output-schema/contract block ('record PASS citing the inspected file when nothing in this role's domain appears in it; PARTIAL and FAIL are reserved for a defect actually found'), and leave expected_evidence as the per-item, file-specific `inspect file: <path>`. Retarget §7 item 7 to assert the rule appears once in each non-spec-coverage prompt's output-contract block rather than in every item's expected_evidence, and drop the corresponding sentence from §6's cost accounting.

finding: §2.2 asserts "The wording is part of the emitted contract, not left to sub-agent judgment" but never supplies the wording, and §7 item 7 then asks a test to prove each `expected_evidence` "instructs a `PASS` citing the inspected file" with no token to match. The current value is exactly `"inspect file: " + f.Path` (internal/cli/audit_roles.go:110); nothing says what it becomes, so one engineer asserts a substring `record PASS`, another asserts `nothing in this role's domain`, and a third only checks the string got longer. The claim that the contract is emitted rather than judged is precisely what makes an unpinned string a defect here.

resolved.evidence: §2.2 now gives the paragraph verbatim in a fenced block rather than describing its intent, so §7 item 8 has an exact token to assert and two engineers cannot write incompatible wording.

suggestion: State the required substrings (at minimum: a `PASS` token, the phrase reserving PARTIAL/FAIL for a found defect, and the inspected file path) or give the full sentence template verbatim, the way §7 item 12 pins its token list.

finding: §2.2 makes every out-of-lens file a PASS "citing the inspected file", and claims the wording is "part of the emitted contract, not left to sub-agent judgment". But the output schema rendered into the same prompt requires BOTH `evidence_file` and `evidence_lines` ("42-58" or "42") to be non-null for PASS, and a "nothing in my domain appears here" verdict has no line range to cite. The spec names the file but not the lines, so exactly the judgment it claims to remove is handed back to the sub-agent, which will either invent a range or emit a schema-invalid row — on most rows of every round in the repositories this release targets.

resolved.evidence: The vacuous-PASS contract gap is closed without touching the schema: the §2.2 paragraph instructs PASS with evidence_file set to the path and evidence_lines set to the full range read (for example '1-120'), which is a truthful assertion — the whole file was inspected and nothing in the role's domain appears — and satisfies renderAuditOutputSchema's requirement that both fields be non-null for PASS. §1 was reworded to 'no change to the audit result schema an auditor returns' so the claim is precise.

suggestion: State what a vacuous PASS puts in `evidence_lines` (e.g. `1-1`, or the file's full range), or say that `evidence_lines` may be null for a file_check PASS and adjust the schema text accordingly — and pin whichever choice in §7 item 7.

finding: §2.2 makes the expected_evidence tell the auditor to "record `PASS` citing the inspected file when nothing in this role's domain appears in it", but the output schema rendered into the same prompt (renderAuditOutputSchema) requires `evidence_lines` — "\"42-58\" (range) or \"42\" (single line) when status is PASS or PARTIAL" — alongside evidence_file. For a file with nothing in the role's domain there is no defect line to cite, so the instruction and the schema disagree about a mandatory field and each auditor invents its own answer (1-1, the whole file range, or an omitted key that fails a strict reader).

resolved.evidence: Same contract gap as the architect's vacuous-pass finding, fixed together: the §2.2 paragraph supplies the evidence_lines value (the full inspected range) that the output schema requires for a PASS, so no field becomes optional and no enum value is added.

suggestion: Say what the nothing-found row puts in evidence_lines (e.g. the first line of the inspected file, or state that evidence_lines may be null for a PASS whose evidence is "file inspected, nothing in domain" and adjust the schema line accordingly), so the item text and the schema block in the same prompt agree.

finding: §2.4's coverage-narrowing note misdescribes the selection being deleted: "a keyword-matching file sorting alphabetically at position 11 through 20 previously reached the security lens". selectSecurity iterates the entire filtered universe and breaks only after 20 *matches* have been collected — it never stops at universe position 20. A matching file at universe position 500 reached the security lens whenever fewer than 20 matches preceded it. The real narrowing is therefore "any keyword-matching file that is not among the first 10 alphabetical universe entries", which is much larger than the stated 10-file window, and §4's documentation is meant to be written from this paragraph.

resolved.evidence: The misdescription is corrected and it changed the design. selectSecurity caps at 20 MATCHES while scanning the entire filtered universe, so a matching file at any universe position reached the lens — making deletion a far larger loss than the spec claimed. §2.4 was rewritten: the keyword list survives as a ranking signal (matching files first, then the rest, each group alphabetical, capped at CodeFileCap) rather than being deleted, so no role can be emptied and matching files survive the cap for every role.

suggestion: Restate the loss precisely: the deleted selection scanned the whole filtered universe and kept up to 20 matches, so after this release any keyword-matching file outside the first CodeFileCap alphabetical universe entries is no longer seen by that lens, regardless of its position.

finding: §2.4's honest-cost paragraph understates the detection loss it is meant to disclose. It says a keyword-matching file "sorting alphabetically at position 11 through 20" previously reached the security lens and no longer does. `selectSecurity` scans the entire filtered universe in alphabetical order and stops at 20 MATCHED entries — the cap bounds matches, not universe position — so today a matching file at universe position 200 is still selected as long as fewer than 20 matches precede it. The real loss is every keyword-matching file outside the first 10 universe entries, which on a large diff is unbounded, not a 10-file window.

resolved.evidence: Same misdescription as the implementer's code-citation-drift finding, and the same fix: §2.4 now ranks rather than filters, which removes most of the loss instead of only disclosing it. The residual narrowing is stated exactly — a matching file beyond the first CodeFileCap of the ranked order no longer reaches any lens, where the old list held up to AuditFileCap matches.

suggestion: Restate the loss as: any keyword-matching file that is not among the first `CodeFileCap` universe files after the drop rules loses the security lens (previously up to 20 matches were selected from anywhere in the universe).

finding: "how many of how many are shown" leaves the denominator undefined, and the two plausible readings differ for spec-coverage. selectSpecCoverage caps the *task-mapped* subset at 20 (falling back to the first 20 filtered-universe files when nothing is task-mapped), so its pre-cap pool is neither the raw universe nor the filtered universe in the normal branch. An implementer must guess between the filtered universe size, the role's own pre-cap candidate set, and the raw --affected-files count; the three routinely disagree and only one makes the truncation claim honest.

resolved.evidence: §2.5 defines both denominators explicitly: CodeFilesTotal is the size of the filtered universe (after the drop rules, since a dropped file was never a candidate), and SpecCoverageTotal is the pool that branch actually capped — the task-mapped set normally, the filtered universe in the no-task fallback.

suggestion: Define the denominator as the size of that role's own pre-cap candidate list after the drop rules (for spec-coverage: the task-mapped set, or the filtered universe in the fallback branch), and say the count is omitted entirely when no truncation occurred.

finding: The new affected-files header is described only behaviorally ("rendered from the cap actually applied", "states how many of how many are shown"), with no literal format, so §7 item 9 has no deterministic assertion — `## Affected Files (max 10)`, `## Affected Files (10 of 23, max 10)` and `## Affected Files (showing 10 of 23)` all satisfy the prose and two engineers write incompatible tests. The denominator is ambiguous too: "the pre-cap universe" could be the raw affected-files/diff universe or the post-`filterAuditUniverse` list, and the two differ whenever a binary, `testdata/**`, `*.golden`, or deleted path is present — exactly the case §2.7 item 2 relies on. A consequence: whether the spec-coverage prompt still contains the literal `## Affected Files (max 20)` that internal/cli/audit_prompts_test.go:33 pins is undecidable from the spec.

resolved.evidence: §2.6 now pins the two literal header forms verbatim, so §7 item 10 asserts exact strings rather than a behavioral description that three different renderings would satisfy.

suggestion: Give the two literal header templates (untruncated and truncated) with one worked example each, and define the denominator explicitly as the file count after the §2.7 drop rules (or before them — but say which).

finding: §2.6 requires the header to state "how many of how many are shown" whenever "the pre-cap universe held more files than the list shows", but the denominator is undefined and, read against the spec's own vocabulary, wrong. §2.5 says the selection rule is "first N universe files after the drop rules", so bare "universe" is the pre-drop list; counting against it would report "10 of 40" when 30 files were dropped as binaries, `testdata/**`, `*.golden`, or deleted — announcing truncation where the cap truncated nothing, the mirror image of the false-completeness bug §2.6 exists to fix. It is also not a single rule across roles: spec-coverage's list is a task-count ranking of the task-mapped subset, not a prefix of the universe.

resolved.evidence: Same ambiguity as the two other §2.6 findings, fixed together in §2.5: the denominator is named as the filtered universe (post-drop-rules), which is the reading this finding argued for, and it is carried as an explicit field rather than inferred from the spec's vocabulary.

suggestion: Name the denominator explicitly as the post-`filterAuditUniverse`, pre-cap candidate set for that role's own selection rule (universe-after-drop-rules for the code-file roles, the task-mapped set — or its universe fallback — for spec-coverage), and state that no count is emitted when the cap dropped nothing.

finding: §2.8 exists to close the round-1 finding that the spec named no fate for the committed tests this change breaks, but its enumeration misses a test that §2.6 puts at risk. internal/cli/audit_prompts_test.go:33 does strings.Index(spec, "## Affected Files (max 20)") on the spec-coverage prompt and then asserts idxFiles >= 0 plus two ordering comparisons (lines 39-43). §2.6 replaces that fixed literal with a header 'rendered from the cap actually applied to that role's list' plus an 'N of M shown' clause, and gives no exact rendered form — so whether the spec-coverage header still reads exactly '## Affected Files (max 20)' is undetermined by the spec, and the ordering test silently depends on it.

resolved.evidence: §2.8 item 6 added: TestAuditPrompts_BodyOrderAndEmbedding's strings.Index on the literal '## Affected Files (max 20)' becomes a prefix match on '## Affected Files (', keeping its ordering assertions intact under §2.6's new header.

suggestion: Add an item to §2.8 naming internal/cli/audit_prompts_test.go's body-order test and stating its fate, and pin the header's rendered form in §2.6 (e.g. '## Affected Files (max <cap>)' with the count clause appended only when the pre-cap universe was larger) so §7 item 9 and the ordering test can both be written against a known string.

finding: §2.8 item 1 ends 'This becomes the regression guard of §6 item 1.' The round-2 revision inserted a new '## 6. Cost' section and renumbered the old '## 6. Tests' to '## 7. Tests', so §6 now has no numbered items at all and the regression guard is §7 item 1. The reference is a renumbering orphan created by the same revision that added §2.8: a reader following it lands in the Cost section. §7 item 1 points back at TestGenerateAuditPrompts_EmptyRoleOmitted correctly, so only one half of the pair is stale.

resolved.evidence: §2.8 item 1's stale '§6 item 1' pointer now reads '§7 item 1'. The round-2 revision that inserted '## 6. Cost' created the orphan; this is exactly the class the regression lens exists to catch.

suggestion: Change '§6 item 1' to '§7 item 1' in §2.8 item 1, and sweep the whole spec for any other §6-as-Tests reference introduced before Cost was inserted.

finding: §2.8 item 2 says TestRouteChecklist_Disjoint "is rewritten against `routeChecklist`'s new single return value", and §7 item 5 asserts "routeChecklist returns that one checklist". The committed test is in package `cli_test` (internal/cli/audit_routing_test.go:1) and is a black-box test that shells the binary through runTP and parses stdout JSON — it never calls routeChecklist and cannot, since the function is unexported in package `cli`. As written the instruction is unimplementable without also moving the test into package `cli` (or adding an export), which the spec does not say.

resolved.evidence: §2.8 item 2 corrected: TestRouteChecklist_Disjoint is a black-box test in package cli_test that shells the binary and parses stdout JSON, so it cannot assert on routeChecklist's return value. It is now specified as rewritten at the same CLI level — spec-derived items only in the spec-coverage prompt, file_check items for every other role.

suggestion: Either restate item 2 and §7 item 5 in observable terms (the emitted spec-coverage prompt carries only table_row/list_item/task_acceptance/finding items and no file_check item; every other role carries only file_check items), or say that a new white-box test in package `cli` covers routeChecklist's single return value while the black-box test is rewritten against prompt output.

finding: §2.8 presents itself as the inventory of tests this change invalidates ("Three committed tests encode the behavior being removed ... and one must be widened"), but at least one further committed test is invalidated and is not listed: `TestAuditPrompts_BodyOrderAndEmbedding` (internal/cli/audit_prompts_test.go) asserts `assert.NotContains(t, sec, "## Project Context")` for the `security` prompt — exactly the assertion §2.3 inverts — and it also indexes the literal header string `"## Affected Files (max 20)"`, which §2.6 replaces with a per-role rendering. A decomposition that trusts §2.8 as exhaustive will hit an unplanned red test.

resolved.evidence: Same incompleteness as the tester's and regression's inventory findings, fixed together: §2.8 is now seven items derived from a named exhaustive search rather than a prose claim of completeness, and TestAuditPrompts_BodyOrderAndEmbedding is item 6.

suggestion: Add `TestAuditPrompts_BodyOrderAndEmbedding` to §2.8 with the two assertions that change (the security Project-Context negative assertion from §2.3, the literal affected-files header from §2.6), or drop the "three tests" framing and state that the list is illustrative.

finding: §3.4 describes the eject advisory only by intent ("states that the written roles are starting points whose focus a project should rewrite for its own stack and conventions") and never gives the line, so §7 item 14's "emits the advisory substring" names a substring the spec does not define — two engineers assert different text and both can claim conformance. The companion claim "The wording names no language" is likewise non-verifiable as stated: no forbidden-token list is given (contrast §7 item 12, which enumerates its tokens), so no deterministic test distinguishes a compliant line from one that says "rewrite the Go specifics".

resolved.evidence: §3.4 now gives the advisory line verbatim in a fenced block, so §7 item 15 asserts that exact string. The domain claim is also made concrete: the wording names no language, which is why the same line is emitted for prose.

suggestion: Quote the advisory line verbatim in §3.4 (or pin the substring §7 item 14 must match), and if the no-language property is to be tested, enumerate the forbidden tokens (`Go`, `PHP`, `TypeScript`, `Ruby`, …) the guard checks.

finding: The documentation guard in §7 item 13 is not writable deterministically from §4. Its positive half — the three files "each state the two-arm routing rule" — names no required substring, so any grep an engineer invents is arbitrary and a doc could pass while saying something else nearby. Its negative half — none "still describes a special file list or item-id scheme for `security` or `maintainability-conventions`" — names no forbidden tokens either, even though §4 itself supplies the obvious candidates (`file-sec-<n>`, `file-maint-<n>`, which live in skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:404 today). Item 12 shows the spec knows how to pin a doc guard; item 13 does not follow it.

resolved.evidence: §4 now names the assertion tokens: every one of the four documents must contain the substring 'spec-coverage is the only reserved auditor id' and must not contain 'file-sec-' or 'file-maint-'. §7 item 14 asserts exactly those tokens, so the guard is writable once and deterministic.

suggestion: Give item 13 the same treatment as item 12: list the forbidden literals (`file-sec-`, `file-maint-`, and any phrase granting `security`/`maintainability-conventions` its own file list) and, for the positive half, a required substring per file (or a single canonical sentence all three must contain).

finding: Non-Goal 3 (added in round 2 to resolve the ejected-corpus finding) rests its whole justification on a claim about §4 that §4 does not carry: '§4's documentation states that the shipped defaults changed, which is the notice.' §4 as revised requires README.md, SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md and CLAUDE.md to state the two-arm ROUTING rule and to drop per-id file-list claims. It says nothing about §3 rewriting the embedded security.json / maintainability-conventions.json focus lines, and §7 item 13's guard test likewise checks only routing wording. So the only notice an already-ejected project (the reporter's own configuration) would ever receive does not exist anywhere in the spec, and the Non-Goal's acceptance cannot be verified.

resolved.evidence: §4 now carries the claim Non-Goal 3 leans on: all four documents must record that the embedded default auditor prompts changed in this release and that an already-ejected corpus keeps its old copies. The cross-reference is supported rather than dangling.

suggestion: Either add the missing requirement to §4 — the docs must also state that the shipped default auditor focus lines changed in this release and that an ejected corpus keeps the old ones until re-ejected with --force — or drop the 'which is the notice' sentence from Non-Goal 3 and state plainly that no notice ships.

finding: The §7 item 12 corpus guard does not cover §3.3's one explicit instructions-field requirement: §3.3 says the `instructions` field "drops the word `idiomatic`", and `idiomatic` is present today (internal/engine/corpus/software/auditors/maintainability-conventions.json:4), yet `idiomatic` is absent from item 12's forbidden token list (`%w`, `0o600`, `0o644`, `camelCase`, `_ = err`, `goroutine`, `lowercase packages`, `files written by the tool`). Separately, item 12 is purely negative: an implementation that emptied or deleted the `focus` arrays of §3.2/§3.3 passes it, so nothing in §7 verifies that the 6 security lines and 5 maintainability lines the spec enumerates actually ship.

resolved.evidence: §7 item 13's deny-list now includes `idiomatic`, so §3.3's instructions-field change is enforced by the same guard that enforces the focus rewrite.

suggestion: Add `idiomatic` to the item 12 token list, and add a positive assertion — e.g. each rewritten auditor's `focus` has the stated item count and each line is non-empty, or pin one distinctive substring per §3.2/§3.3 line — so the rewrite is verified, not only the absence of the old tokens.

finding: §7 item 1 (the headline regression guard) asserts unconditionally that 'every auditor role in the active corpus emits a prompt and skipped_roles is empty' given one affected file matching no security keyword. §2.7, added in the same round, enumerates two skip paths that both remain live under exactly that fixture: spec-coverage is skipped when the spec has no table rows, no numbered list items, no task acceptance and no findings; and every non-spec-coverage role is skipped when the code-file list is empty after the binary/testdata/*.golden/deleted drop rules. The resolution recorded for the round-1 finding claims item 1 'is now scoped to the case where at least one code file survives the drop rules', but no such qualifier was actually written into item 1 — its wording is unchanged from round 1 apart from the appended EmptyRoleOmitted note. As written §7 item 1 contradicts §2.7, and an implementer whose fixture trips either path may 'fix' the guard by weakening it.

resolved.evidence: §7 item 1 now states its precondition: the fixture spec has structured elements so spec-coverage earns a checklist, which is what makes 'skipped_roles is empty' achievable given §2.7's two live skip paths.

suggestion: Scope item 1 explicitly: 'Given a spec with at least one structured element and one affected code file that survives the universe filter and whose path and content match no security keyword, every auditor role emits a prompt and skipped_roles is empty.' §7 items 10 and 11 already cover the two skip cases separately.

finding: §7 item 13 specifies a guard test that asserts README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md and skills/tp/REFERENCE.md "each state the two-arm routing rule" and that "none of them still describes a special file list or item-id scheme", but unlike item 12 — which enumerates its forbidden substrings exactly — item 13 supplies neither the required substring nor the forbidden ones. An implementer must invent both the canonical doc sentence and the assertion, so the doc task and the test task can diverge silently. §4 additionally requires the CLAUDE.md role-corpus rule to tell the same story, yet CLAUDE.md is absent from the guard's file list without a stated reason.

resolved.evidence: Same gap as the tester's unpinned-assertion-token finding, fixed together: §4 supplies the required and forbidden substrings and §7 item 14 enumerates them exactly, matching the precision of item 13.

suggestion: Give item 13 the same treatment as item 12: name the marker substring every doc must contain (e.g. "spec-coverage is the only reserved auditor id") and the forbidden substrings (`file-sec-`, `file-maint-`, and any phrase attaching a special file list to `security`/`maintainability-conventions`), and state whether CLAUDE.md is in or out of the guard.

finding: Deleting the `security` and `maintainability-conventions` switch arms (§2.1) and the CLAUDE.md id gate (§2.3) removes the last uses of the `roleSecurity` and `roleMaintainability` constants (internal/cli/audit_roles.go:20-21) — routeChecklist:54-55, the switch at :286/:288 and buildRolePrompt:220 are the only readers. .golangci.yml enables `unused`, which reports unused unexported constants, so the implementing commit fails the `golangci-lint run` half of the quality gate. §2.4 enumerates the engine symbols that go away but says nothing about these two.

resolved.evidence: Same as the architect's incomplete-removal-inventory finding: §2.1 states both constants are deleted, so the enabled `unused` linter does not fail the quality gate on symbols the change orphans.

suggestion: Add the two constants to the removal list (keeping `roleSpecCoverage`, which stays in use), or state that they remain and are referenced by the surviving spec-coverage checks.

finding: Round 1 removed the absolute 'no id is treated specially' phrasing from §4 because it contradicted spec-coverage staying reserved; §4 now correctly says 'spec-coverage is the single reserved id'. The same absolute framing survived the rewrite in §2.1 and was carried into §7 item 2: §2.1 claims 'a role named security and an identically-authored role under ANY OTHER ID receive the same number of items over the same files', and §7 item 2 says 'security versus any other id'. Instantiated with the id spec-coverage — which is another id — both statements are false by §2.1's own first paragraph, so the fix landed in one section and not in its two siblings.

resolved.evidence: §2.1's absolute framing is gone. The claim now reads 'no id other than spec-coverage changes any part of prompt construction', matching §4's 'spec-coverage is the single reserved id' rather than contradicting it.

suggestion: Say 'under any other non-reserved id (any id other than spec-coverage)' in §2.1's observable-consequence paragraph and in §7 item 2.

finding: §2.3 widens the `## Project Context` block from one role to every non-spec-coverage role and justifies the cost as 'up to 50 lines of project conventions', but claudeMDExcerptFor/claudeConventionsExcerpt only yields conventions when CLAUDE.md contains a literal `## Conventions` heading; otherwise it falls back to the file's first 50 lines. In a project without that heading the block is whatever opens CLAUDE.md — title, install steps, tech stack — and the change multiplies that non-decision-feeding payload by the number of auditor roles on every round of a 2-consecutive-clean gate, while the field report this release answers comes from exactly such a foreign repository. The spec's cost paragraph (§6) inherits the same unconditional 'project conventions' framing, so the accounting reads cheaper than the worst case.

resolved.evidence: §2.3 now states the fallback explicitly: claudeMDExcerptFor yields the ## Conventions section when that heading exists and otherwise the file's first 50 lines, so in a project without the heading the block carries the opening 50 lines instead of conventions. The fallback is flagged as pre-existing and unchanged, and the 50-line cap is named as what bounds the cost either way.

suggestion: Scope the widened block to the case that earns it: attach `## Project Context` to the shared-arm roles only when the `## Conventions` section was actually found, and emit nothing when the excerpt is the first-N-lines fallback (the maintainability-conventions role's existing behavior can stay unchanged if regression cover matters). If the fallback is deliberately kept, say so in §2.3 and restate §6's delta as 'up to 50 lines of CLAUDE.md — the ## Conventions section when present, otherwise the file's opening lines' so the cost is not undersold.

finding: §2.4 defers to "the role-declared file selection of §5.1". §5 (Non-Goals) is a flat numbered list with no subsections, so §5.1 resolves to nothing; the intended target is §5 item 1 ("Role-declared file selection"). §5 was rewritten in this revision (now 7 items), so the dangling reference now points into a renumbered list.

resolved.evidence: The dangling '§5.1' now reads '§5 item 1', since §5 is a flat numbered list with no subsections.

suggestion: Write "§5 item 1" (or give Non-Goals real subsections) so the reference resolves.

finding: §2.8 item 1 says the inverted `TestGenerateAuditPrompts_EmptyRoleOmitted` "becomes the regression guard of §6 item 1". That reference was correct before this revision, when §6 was the Tests section; the revision inserted "## 6. Cost" and moved Tests to §7, so §6 now has no numbered items and the pointer lands in the cost discussion. §7 item 1 is the intended target.

resolved.evidence: Same renumbering orphan as the regression lens's stale-section-reference finding: §2.8 item 1 now points at §7 item 1.

suggestion: Change "§6 item 1" to "§7 item 1" and sweep the spec for other section-number references that moved when §6 Cost was inserted.

finding: §2.8's lead sentence ("Three committed tests encode the behavior being removed ... and one must be widened") does not match its own list: four numbered items name five test functions, and it is not stated which one is the widened one. Item 3's "the remaining assertions in that file are renamed mechanically to CodeFiles and CodeFileCap" is also inaccurate — TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted (internal/engine/auditfiles_test.go:125) contains `assert.Empty(t, sel.Security)`, which must be deleted rather than renamed, and TestFilterFiles_Maintainability keeps a function name derived from the field being renamed.

resolved.evidence: §2.8's preamble no longer miscounts: it states the inventory is exhaustive against a named search and lists seven items, dropping the 'three tests and one widening' framing that did not match its own list. Item 4 now says the sel.Security assertion in TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted is deleted rather than renamed.

suggestion: Drop the count from the lead (or fix it to four items / five functions), mark which item is the widening, and note in item 3 that the surviving sel.Security assertion in TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted is deleted and that the TestFilterFiles_Maintainability name is (or is not) renamed with the field.

finding: §2.8's preamble says 'Three committed tests encode the behavior being removed and must change with it, and one must be widened because its current scope would let the defect return', then lists four items none of which is a widening: item 4 (TestGenerateAuditPrompts_CLAUDEmdOnlyForMaintainability) pins the id gate §2.3 removes and is rewritten, i.e. it is a fourth test encoding removed behavior. The widening the preamble refers to is §7 item 2 (item-count equality widened to full prompt equality), which lives in a different section. The count is also off: item 3 names two tests (TestFilterFiles_Security and the security half of TestFilterFiles_Cap20) plus a file-wide rename, so four or five tests change, not three.

resolved.evidence: Same count mismatch as the implementer's test-inventory-drift finding, fixed together: the preamble's arithmetic claim is replaced by the search that makes the list verifiable.

suggestion: Rewrite the preamble as 'Four committed tests encode behavior this change removes and must change with it' and move the widening note to §7 item 2, where the widened assertion actually lives.

finding: §3.3 states a second change beyond the focus rewrite — the `instructions` field "drops the word `idiomatic` in favour of naming the project's own conventions as the standard" — but unlike the five focus lines it gives no replacement text, and no §7 test pins it: the §7 item 12 guard bans `%w`, `0o600`, `camelCase`, `_ = err` and friends, but not `idiomatic`. §3.2 is silent about `security.json`'s `instructions` string for the same reason, so the two subsections are asymmetric about which fields they govern.

resolved.evidence: §3.3 now gives the replacement instructions clause verbatim ('only whether the code is maintainable and consistent with the conventions already present in this project'), and §7 item 13's deny-list gained `idiomatic` so the change is pinned. §3.2 now states security.json's instructions field is already neutral and unchanged, closing the silence this finding noted.

suggestion: Give the replacement `instructions` sentence verbatim (as §3.2/§3.3 do for focus lines) and add `idiomatic` to the §7 item 12 banned-substring list, or state that `instructions` wording is task-acceptance detail and drop the claim from §3.3.

finding: §4 requires four documents — README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md, and the role-corpus rule in CLAUDE.md — to "all tell one story" about the routing contract, but §7 item 13's guard test covers only the first three. CLAUDE.md is therefore the one required document that can silently drift, and it is the document §2.3 newly wires into the audit loop itself: its `## Conventions` excerpt is now injected into every non-spec-coverage prompt.

resolved.evidence: Same scope gap as the regression lens's guard-scope finding: §7 item 14 now covers CLAUDE.md alongside README.md, SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md, so the document a self-development agent reads every session cannot drift silently.

suggestion: Either include CLAUDE.md in the §7 item 13 guard, or state in §4 that CLAUDE.md is updated but deliberately not machine-guarded, with the reason.

finding: Round 1 killed the false 'Removing the heuristic does not widen the token budget' claim, but §6 reintroduces a weaker version of it: 'In a repository where the heuristic already matched, cost does not rise'. Two sentences later the same section states that §2.3 adds up to 50 lines of project conventions to EACH non-spec-coverage prompt and §2.6 adds a count to a header — deltas that apply to the already-matching repository too. The flat 'cost does not rise' is therefore contradicted by the section's own next paragraph.

resolved.evidence: §6 rewritten. The weaker 'cost does not rise' claim is gone; it now says the file count per prompt falls from up to 20 to up to 10 while §2.3 adds up to 50 conventions lines and §2.6 a header count, that net prompt size is roughly unchanged, and that the release trades a narrower file list for a wider role panel without claiming to be free anywhere.

suggestion: Qualify the claim to the thing it is actually true of: 'the per-role file list does not grow — the shared list caps at 10 where the security list capped at 20 — and no additional role prompt is emitted', then let the 'two smaller deltas' paragraph state what does grow in every repository.

finding: §2.7 and §7 item 10 both say the audit "exit code is unchanged" without ever naming it, so the assertion is relative to an unstated baseline. The prompt's own checklist asks for exit codes to be pinned (0/1/2/3/4); every other numeric contract in this spec (caps 10 and 20, the 50-line excerpt) is given as a literal.

resolved.evidence: §2.7 and §7 item 11 now name the exit code as the literal 0, matching how every other numeric contract in this spec is stated.

suggestion: State the literal — a prompt-emitting `tp audit` run that skips roles still exits 0 — in §2.7 and in §7 item 10.

finding: §7 item 13 was added to make §4 verifiable, but it guards three of §4's four documents: §4 requires README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md and 'the role-corpus rule in CLAUDE.md' to tell one story, while the guard test asserts only on README.md, SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md. CLAUDE.md's role-corpus rule is the one doc that a self-development agent reads on every session, and it is left free to keep or regrow a per-id routing claim without failing the gate.

resolved.evidence: Same scope gap as the architect's guard-scope finding, fixed together in §7 item 14, which now asserts all four documents §4 names.

suggestion: Either add CLAUDE.md to the guard test's file list in §7 item 13, or state in §4 why CLAUDE.md is deliberately excluded from the assertion.
